stem.en: Kabir asks why the Rr seed is "fully round, not half round, since it has only half the working genes". What does the flip show?

text.en: One working copy makes enough branching enzyme to branch all the starch, because enzymes are catalysts and are not used up, from V.4. Half the enzyme does the whole job a little slower. So the phenotype is the same as RR. That is why R is dominant.
It is half round; Mendel did not look closely.

feedback.en: Mendel's hybrids were as round as the pure line. The starch in the sim's Rr seed is fully branched.

text.en: The R copy repairs the r copy.

feedback.en: Nothing repairs the r spelling. It stays broken and is passed on. The R copy simply does the job alone.

text.en: The seed uses only the R copy.

feedback.en: Both are read. The r message makes a useless protein, and the R message makes enough.

explanation.en: Dominance is often just this: one working copy of an enzyme suffices. A catalyst is not used up, so a double amount buys nothing.
